questions.q: What best describes a tabular report?
options: A flat list with one row per record and no grouping
A report grouped by rows with subtotals
A report grouped by both rows and columns
Multiple report blocks shown side by side
questions.explain: Tabular reports are simple flat tables of records. Grouping and subtotals belong to the Summary format.

questions.q: Which SQL statement is closest to a tabular report?
options: SELECT Owner, SUM(Amount) FROM Opportunity GROUP BY Owner
SELECT Name, Type, Rating FROM Account WHERE Rating = 'Hot' ORDER BY Name
SELECT ... FROM A UNION SELECT ... FROM B
SELECT ... OVER (PARTITION BY Owner)
questions.explain: A tabular report has columns, filters, and sorting but no aggregation, which matches a plain SELECT with WHERE and ORDER BY.

questions.q: A tabular report can generally feed a dashboard component only if...
options: It has at least three columns
It is saved in a private folder
You set a row limit on the report
It contains a Date field
questions.explain: Without groupings, a tabular report needs a row limit (such as top 10) before a dashboard component can use it.

questions.q: You run a tabular report and Total Records is far higher than you expected. What is the most sensible first check?
options: Switch the report to Joined
Review the filters, since one is probably missing or wrong
Delete the report and start over with a different object
Add a chart
questions.explain: Total Records is a quick sanity check. An unexpectedly large count usually means a filter is missing, too broad, or set to All Time.

questions.q: Which task is a good fit for a tabular report?
options: Total pipeline broken down by sales rep and by month
A call list of hot accounts to be exported to a spreadsheet
Comparing two different report types in one view
A chart of cases by priority
questions.explain: Lists and exports are tabular's strength. Breakdowns and charts need grouping (Summary or Matrix), and comparing report types needs Joined.
